Take an emoji apart: base, skin tone, gender and hair

Source: R/emoji-identity.R
emoji_decompose.Rd

emoji_decompose() reports, for each glyph, what it depicts of a person and how it is built: the emoji with its skin tones taken out, its gender-neutral form, its tones, the gender and hair it shows, and the components it is joined from. It describes glyphs, never the people who write them; see Glyphs, not people in tidyEmoji. It is what emoji_skin_tone(), emoji_gender() and emoji_retone() read.

Usage

emoji_decompose(x, long = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A character vector of glyphs.

long

If TRUE, return one row per component instead, the way emoji_emotion() does: emoji, position, component, role ("person", "object", "gender_sign", "hair", "tone" or "other") and component_name.

Value

With long = FALSE, a tibble with one row per element of x: emoji (as given), name, base, neutral, tone, tones, n_tones (distinct tones), gender, hair ("red", "curly", "white" or "bald", NA otherwise), n_parts (the components a zero-width joiner joins, 1 for a glyph with no joiner), parts (those components without their tones, separated by "|") and modifiable (whether the base takes a tone). NA input gives a row of NA.

Details

Each glyph is canonicalised first, so the bare heart U+2764 and the qualified U+2764 U+FE0F decompose alike, and read from a table the package builds once per session over the catalogue; a glyph the catalogue does not list, such as a face followed by a swatch it cannot take, is worked out on the fly.

  • Tone is "default" for a glyph that takes a tone and has none, "light", "medium_light", "medium", "medium_dark" or "dark" for one tone however many people carry it, and "mixed" for two or more, as on a couple with two tones. It is NA only where the glyph cannot take a tone. tones lists every tone in reading order.

  • Gender is the one the glyph is drawn with: "female" or "male" from the female and male signs U+2640 and U+2642 or a gendered person (woman, man, girl, boy, old woman, old man), and from a list of twelve emoji whose gender lives in one code point (prince and princess, Santa and Mrs. Claus, the two dancers, the two pregnant people, men and women holding hands, the woman with headscarf, and breast-feeding, which the list follows emojibase in calling female); "mixed" for a multi-person emoji with both, a derivation of this package's own; "neutral" for the gender-neutral form, which platforms draw differently; NA where no gender is depicted.

  • Neutral is the gender-neutral form the catalogue has, so woman running gives person running and woman technologist gives technologist; NA where there is none.

  • Base is the glyph with every tone taken out, in the catalogue's spelling. For a two-person emoji written as one code point untoned, a kiss or a handshake, the toned spellings are joined sequences and the base is the single code point.

See also

emoji_skin_tone(), emoji_gender() and emoji_retone(), which apply it to a text column; emoji_properties() for what the catalogue records.

Examples

couple <- "\U0001f469\U0001f3fb\u200d\u2764\ufe0f\u200d\U0001f468\U0001f3ff"
emoji_decompose(c("\U0001f44d\U0001f3fd", couple, "\U0001f3c3\u200d\u2640\ufe0f"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 12
#>   emoji name        base  neutral tone  tones n_tones gender hair  n_parts parts
#>   <chr> <chr>       <chr> <chr>   <chr> <chr>   <int> <chr>  <chr>   <int> <chr>
#> 1 👍🏽    thumbs up:… 👍    NA      medi… medi…       1 NA     NA          1 👍   
#> 2 👩🏻‍❤️‍👨🏿    couple wit… 👩‍❤️‍👨    💑      mixed ligh…       2 mixed  NA          3 👩|❤️|…
#> 3 🏃‍♀️    woman runn… 🏃‍♀️    🏃      defa… defa…       0 female NA          2 🏃|♀️ 
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: modifiable <lgl>
emoji_decompose(couple, long = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   emoji position component role   component_name 
#>   <chr>    <int> <chr>     <chr>  <chr>          
#> 1 👩🏻‍❤️‍👨🏿           1 👩        person woman          
#> 2 👩🏻‍❤️‍👨🏿           2 🏻        tone   light skin tone
#> 3 👩🏻‍❤️‍👨🏿           3 ❤️         object red heart      
#> 4 👩🏻‍❤️‍👨🏿           4 👨        person man            
#> 5 👩🏻‍❤️‍👨🏿           5 🏿        tone   dark skin tone
